parts.label: a
hints: The y-coordinate of a point on the cumulative frequency curve indicates the count of values at or below that x-value.
To find the count strictly above $54$, subtract the cumulative total from the total number of students: $160 - 112 = 48$.

walkthrough.text:
Read the count of students scoring at most 54 marks from the y-coordinate:
$$\text{Count}(\le 54) = CF(54) = 112\text{ students}$$

Subtract the cumulative frequency from the total sample size to find the upper tail count:
$$\text{Count}(> 54) = N - CF(54) = 160 - 112 = 48\text{ students}$$

teacher_walkthrough.text:
Read directly from the curve coordinate:
$$\text{At most 54: } 112$$

Subtract from total for the remainder:
$$160 - 112 = 48$$

ai_rubric.observable: State that 112 students scored at most 54 marks.
Calculate number scoring more than 54 marks as 160 - 112 = 48 students.

parts.label: a
hints: To find the count between two values, subtract the lower cumulative reading from the upper cumulative reading: $94 - 28$.
Divide the count by the total sample size $120$ and multiply by $100$ to obtain the percentage: $(66 / 120) \times 100 = 55\%$.

walkthrough.text:
Calculate the frequency in the interval $[30, 60]$ by subtracting cumulative totals:
$$\text{Count}(30 \le x \le 60) = CF(60) - CF(30) = 94 - 28 = 66\text{ batteries}$$

Convert this count to a percentage of the total sample of 120 batteries:
$$\text{Percentage} = \frac{66}{120} \times 100\% = 55\%$$

teacher_walkthrough.text:
Take the difference between the two cumulative readings:
$$94 - 28 = 66$$

ai_rubric.observable: Calculate count between 30 and 60 hours: 94 - 28 = 66.
Calculate percentage as (66 / 120) * 100 = 55%.

parts.label: a
hints: The lower quartile $Q_1$ corresponds to one quarter of the total frequency: $0.25 \times N$.
The upper quartile $Q_3$ corresponds to three quarters of the total frequency: $0.75 \times N$.

walkthrough.text:
Calculate the cumulative frequency position for the lower quartile:
$$CF(Q_1) = \frac{1}{4} N = 0.25 \times 200 = 50$$

Calculate the cumulative frequency position for the upper quartile:
$$CF(Q_3) = \frac{3}{4} N = 0.75 \times 200 = 150$$

ai_rubric.observable: Calculate Q1 target cumulative frequency as 0.25 * 200 = 50.
Calculate Q3 target cumulative frequency as 0.75 * 200 = 150.

parts.label: a
hints: The interquartile range is the difference between upper and lower quartiles: $Q_3 - Q_1$.
Evaluate $38.0 - 24.5 = 13.5\text{ minutes}$, and explain that it represents the spread of the middle half of the distribution.

walkthrough.text:
Calculate the interquartile range from the quartile readings:
$$\text{IQR} = Q_3 - Q_1 = 38.0 - 24.5 = 13.5\text{ minutes}$$

Interpret the meaning of the interquartile range in context:
$$\text{The spread of the middle } 50\% \text{ of runners' race times is } 13.5\text{ minutes}$$

teacher_walkthrough.text:
State the statistical interpretation:
$$\text{The middle 50% of runners span a range of 13.5 minutes.}$$

ai_rubric.observable: Calculate IQR = 38.0 - 24.5 = 13.5 minutes.
Interpret IQR as the range of the middle 50% of runners' race times.

parts.label: a
hints: Calculate $85\%$ of the total sample size: $0.85 \times 240$.
A percentile is a data score read on the horizontal axis corresponding to that cumulative frequency, not the count itself.

walkthrough.text:
Compute target cumulative frequency for the 85th percentile:
$$\text{Target } CF = 0.85 \times N = 0.85 \times 240 = 204$$

Clarify the nature of a percentile:
$$\text{The 85th percentile is the mark value read on the horizontal axis at } CF = 204$$

teacher_walkthrough.text:
Distinguish between input and output on the graph:
$$\text{The percentile is the mark score on the x-axis, not 204.}$$

ai_rubric.observable: Calculate target cumulative frequency as 0.85 * 240 = 204.
State that the percentile is a mark value read on the horizontal axis (not a frequency count).

parts.label: a
hints: Since the cumulative frequency curve counts from the bottom upwards, subtract the upper tail percentage from $100\%$.

walkthrough.text:
Take the complement of the upper-tail percentage:
$$\text{Cumulative percentage} = 100\% - 20\% = 80\%$$

Calculate target cumulative frequency for the 80th percentile:
$$\text{Target } CF = 0.80 \times 150 = 120$$

teacher_walkthrough.text:
Find the percentage at or below V:
$$100\% - 20\% = 80\%$$

ai_rubric.observable: State cumulative percentage as 100% - 20% = 80%.
Calculate target cumulative frequency as 0.80 * 150 = 120.

parts.label: a
hints: Read the cumulative frequency directly at $x = 25$ from the point $(25, 63)$.
To find commuters taking longer than $40$ minutes, subtract the cumulative total at $40$ from the total $180$: $180 - 135 = 45$.

walkthrough.text:
Determine the number of commuters with journey time at most 25 minutes:
$$\text{Count}(\le 25) = CF(25) = 63\text{ commuters}$$

Determine the number of commuters with journey time exceeding 40 minutes:
$$\text{Count}(> 40) = 180 - CF(40) = 180 - 135 = 45\text{ commuters}$$

teacher_walkthrough.text:
Read the count at 25 minutes:
$$\text{At most 25 min: } 63$$

Subtract count at 40 minutes from total:
$$180 - 135 = 45$$

ai_rubric.observable: Read number with journey time at most 25 minutes as 63 commuters.
Calculate number with journey time exceeding 40 minutes as 180 - 135 = 45 commuters.

parts.label: b
hints: Subtract the cumulative frequency at $15$ from the cumulative frequency at $40$: $135 - 24$.
Divide $111$ by the total count $180$ and simplify by dividing numerator and denominator by $3$.

walkthrough.text:
Calculate the count between 15 and 40 minutes:
$$\text{Count}(15 \le t \le 40) = CF(40) - CF(15) = 135 - 24 = 111\text{ commuters}$$

Simplify the fraction of the total sample:
$$\text{Fraction} = \frac{111}{180} = \frac{37}{60}$$

teacher_walkthrough.text:
Find the difference between 40 min and 15 min readings:
$$135 - 24 = 111$$

ai_rubric.observable: Calculate number between 15 and 40 minutes as 135 - 24 = 111 commuters.
Express as fraction of total: 111 / 180 = 37 / 60.

parts.label: a
hints: The median corresponds to $CF = 0.50 \times 120 = 60$, so read the x-value at $CF = 60$.
The lower quartile $Q_1$ corresponds to $CF = 0.25 \times 120 = 30$, so read the x-value at $CF = 30$.

walkthrough.text:
Identify the median revenue at the 50% cumulative frequency position ($CF = 60$):
$$\text{Median} = x(60) = 27\text{ hundred dollars}$$

Identify the lower quartile at the 25% cumulative frequency position ($CF = 30$):
$$Q_1 = x(30) = 18\text{ hundred dollars}$$

ai_rubric.observable: Identify median as 27 hundred dollars (at CF = 60).
Identify lower quartile Q1 as 18 hundred dollars (at CF = 30).

parts.label: b
hints: The upper quartile $Q_3$ is located at $CF = 0.75 \times 120 = 90$, where $x = 38$ hundred dollars.
Compute $\text{IQR} = Q_3 - Q_1 = 38 - 18 = 20\text{ hundred dollars}$, which equals $20 \times 100 = 2000\text{ dollars}$.

walkthrough.text:
Identify the upper quartile from the reading at $CF = 90$:
$$Q_3 = x(90) = 38\text{ hundred dollars}$$

Calculate the interquartile range in units of hundreds of dollars:
$$\text{IQR} = Q_3 - Q_1 = 38 - 18 = 20\text{ hundred dollars}$$

Convert the interquartile range to dollars:
$$\text{Middle 50% spread} = 20 \times 100 = 2000\text{ dollars}$$

ai_rubric.observable: State Q3 = 38 hundred dollars (at CF = 90).
Calculate IQR = 38 - 18 = 20 hundred dollars.
Convert to actual dollars: 20 * 100 = 2000 dollars.

parts.label: a
hints: Find the target cumulative frequency for the 30th percentile: $0.30 \times 150 = 45$.
The cumulative frequency $45$ corresponds to a plant height of $18\text{ cm}$.
For plants taller than $32\text{ cm}$, subtract the cumulative frequency $120$ from $150$, then divide by $150$ and multiply by $100$: $(30 / 150) \times 100 = 20\%$.

walkthrough.text:
Locate the 30th percentile at $CF = 0.30 \times 150 = 45$:
$$P_{30} = 18\text{ cm}$$

Calculate the percentage of plants exceeding 32 cm:
$$\text{Percentage} = \frac{150 - 120}{150} \times 100\% = \frac{30}{150} \times 100\% = 20\%$$

teacher_walkthrough.text:
Match 30% of 150 to cumulative frequency 45:
$$P_{30} = 18\text{ cm}$$

Find upper tail percentage above 32 cm:
$$\frac{150 - 120}{150} \times 100\% = 20\%$$

ai_rubric.observable: Identify 30th percentile target as 0.30 * 150 = 45, giving height = 18 cm.
Calculate percentage taller than 32 cm as ((150 - 120) / 150) * 100 = 20%.

parts.label: b
hints: The top $10\%$ boundary corresponds to the 90th percentile: $100\% - 10\% = 90\%$.
Compare $CF = 135$ with $CF = 120$ (at $32\text{ cm}$): since cumulative frequency curves are non-decreasing, a higher cumulative total requires a larger x-value.

walkthrough.text:
Find the cumulative frequency index for the top 10% threshold (90th percentile):
$$\text{Target } CF = (1 - 0.10) \times 150 = 0.90 \times 150 = 135$$

Compare this target cumulative frequency to the 80th percentile position:
$$CF_{90} = 135 > 120 = CF_{80}$$

Deduce that the minimum tall plant height exceeds 32 cm:
$$\text{Since } CF(x) \text{ is monotonically increasing, } CF = 135 \implies x > 32\text{ cm}$$

teacher_walkthrough.text:
Reason using the increasing curve property:
$$\text{A higher cumulative rank corresponds to a greater height than 32 cm.}$$

ai_rubric.observable: Calculate target cumulative frequency as 0.90 * 150 = 135.
Note that CF = 135 > 120 (the 80th percentile at 32 cm).
Conclude that since cumulative frequency is monotonically increasing, the height at CF = 135 must be strictly greater than 32 cm.

parts.label: a
hints: Lower quartile is at $CF = 0.25 \times 200 = 50$, which lies between $(40, 30)$ and $(60, 90)$.
Median is at $CF = 0.50 \times 200 = 100$, which lies between $(60, 90)$ and $(80, 160)$.

ai_rubric.observable: Interpolate Q1 at CF = 50: 40 + (20 / 60) * 20.
Interpolate median at CF = 100: 60 + (10 / 70) * 20 = 62.9 (or 440/7).

parts.label: b
hints: Interpolate cumulative frequency at score $75$ between $x = 60$ ($CF = 90$) and $x = 80$ ($CF = 160$).
The number scoring more than $75$ is $200 - 142.5 = 57.5$.
Convert to percentage: $(57.5 / 200) \times 100 = 28.75\%$.

walkthrough.text:
Interpolate cumulative frequency at $S = 75$:
$$CF(75) = 90 + \frac{75 - 60}{80 - 60} \times (160 - 90) = 90 + \frac{15}{20} \times 70 = 90 + 52.5 = 142.5$$

Calculate the count of applicants scoring greater than 75:
$$\text{Count}(> 75) = 200 - 142.5 = 57.5$$

Calculate the percentage exceeding 75 marks:
$$\text{Percentage} = \frac{57.5}{200} \times 100\% = 28.75\%$$

ai_rubric.observable: Set up linear interpolation for CF at S = 75: 90 + (15 / 20) * 70.
Obtain CF(75) = 142.5 (accept 142 or 143).
Calculate percentage scoring greater than 75 as ((200 - 142.5) / 200) * 100 = 28.75% (or 28.8%).

parts.label: a
hints: Subtract the lower quartile from the upper quartile: $Q_3 - Q_1 = 63.5 - 48.0$.
The semi-interquartile range is half of the interquartile range: $\frac{1}{2} \times \text{IQR}$.
Evaluate $15.5 / 2 = 7.75\text{ kg}$.

walkthrough.text:
Calculate the interquartile range:
$$\text{IQR} = Q_3 - Q_1 = 63.5 - 48.0 = 15.5\text{ kg}$$

Calculate the semi-interquartile range:
$$\text{Semi-IQR} = \frac{\text{IQR}}{2} = \frac{15.5}{2} = 7.75\text{ kg}$$

teacher_walkthrough.text:
Find the difference between Q3 and Q1:
$$\text{IQR} = 63.5 - 48.0 = 15.5\text{ kg}$$

ai_rubric.observable: Calculate IQR = Q3 - Q1 = 63.5 - 48.0.
Obtain IQR = 15.5 kg.
Calculate semi-interquartile range = 15.5 / 2 = 7.75 kg.

parts.label: b
hints: Multiply the IQR by $1.5$: $1.5 \times 15.5 = 23.25\text{ kg}$.
Subtract $23.25$ from $Q_1 = 48.0$ to find the lower outlier boundary.
Add $23.25$ to $Q_3 = 63.5$ to find the upper outlier boundary.
The boundaries are $24.75\text{ kg}$ and $86.75\text{ kg}$.

walkthrough.text:
Calculate the outlier step size:
$$1.5 \times \text{IQR} = 1.5 \times 15.5 = 23.25\text{ kg}$$

Calculate the lower outlier boundary:
$$\text{Lower threshold} = Q_1 - 1.5 \times \text{IQR} = 48.0 - 23.25 = 24.75\text{ kg}$$

Calculate the upper outlier boundary:
$$\text{Upper threshold} = Q_3 + 1.5 \times \text{IQR} = 63.5 + 23.25 = 86.75\text{ kg}$$

teacher_walkthrough.text:
Subtract from Q1 for lower boundary:
$$48.0 - 23.25 = 24.75\text{ kg}$$

Add to Q3 for upper boundary:
$$63.5 + 23.25 = 86.75\text{ kg}$$

ai_rubric.observable: Calculate lower threshold: 48.0 - 23.25 = 24.75 kg.
Calculate upper threshold: 63.5 + 23.25 = 86.75 kg.

parts.label: a
hints: The starting point $(150, 0)$ gives the lower boundary of the lowest class, where cumulative frequency is zero.
Therefore, the minimum recorded reaction time is $150\text{ ms}$.
To find the count between $200\text{ ms}$ and $360\text{ ms}$, subtract cumulative frequencies: $CF(360) - CF(200) = 222 - 36$.
Compute $222 - 36 = 186\text{ participants}$.

walkthrough.text:
Identify the minimum reaction time from the baseline origin:
$$\text{Starting point} = (150, 0) \implies \text{Minimum reaction time} = 150\text{ ms}$$

Calculate participants with reaction times between 200 ms and 360 ms:
$$\text{Count}(200 \le t \le 360) = CF(360) - CF(200) = 222 - 36 = 186\text{ participants}$$

teacher_walkthrough.text:
Read the baseline value:
$$\text{Min time} = 150\text{ ms}$$

ai_rubric.observable: Identify minimum reaction time as 150 ms (from start coordinate (150, 0)).
Calculate count between 200 ms and 360 ms as 222 - 36 = 186 participants.

parts.label: b
hints: Lower quartile is at $CF = 0.25 \times 240 = 60$, between $(200, 36)$ and $(250, 108)$.
Upper quartile is at $CF = 0.75 \times 240 = 180$, between $(250, 108)$ and $(300, 186)$.

walkthrough.text:
Interpolate lower quartile $Q_1$ at $CF = 0.25 \times 240 = 60$:
$$Q_1 = 200 + \frac{60 - 36}{108 - 36} \times (250 - 200) = 200 + \frac{24}{72} \times 50 = 200 + \frac{50}{3} \approx 216.7\text{ ms}$$

Interpolate upper quartile $Q_3$ at $CF = 0.75 \times 240 = 180$:
$$Q_3 = 250 + \frac{180 - 108}{186 - 108} \times (300 - 250) = 250 + \frac{72}{78} \times 50 = 250 + \frac{600}{13} \approx 296.2\text{ ms}$$

teacher_walkthrough.text:
Interpolate Q1 at cumulative count 60:
$$Q_1 = 200 + \frac{24}{72} \times 50 \approx 216.7\text{ ms}$$

Interpolate Q3 at cumulative count 180:
$$Q_3 = 250 + \frac{72}{78} \times 50 \approx 296.2\text{ ms}$$

ai_rubric.observable: Interpolate Q1 at CF = 60: 200 + (24 / 72) * 50.
Obtain Q1 = 216.7 ms (accept 217 ms or 650/3).
Interpolate Q3 at CF = 180: 250 + (72 / 78) * 50 = 296.2 ms (accept 296 ms or 3850/13).

parts.label: c
hints: Faster reaction times are represented by shorter times (lower values on the horizontal axis).
The fastest $15\%$ of participants occupy the bottom $15\%$ of the distribution: $0.15 \times 240 = 36$.
Check the given coordinates: the curve passes directly through $(200, 36)$.
At cumulative frequency $36$, the reaction time is exactly $200\text{ ms}$.
The maximum qualifying reaction time is $200\text{ ms}$.

walkthrough.text:
Interpret 'fastest 15%' in terms of reaction time magnitude:
$$\text{Fastest reaction times are the shortest times} \implies \text{Lower tail cutoff at } 0.15 \times 240 = 36$$

Read the exact coordinate corresponding to $CF = 36$:
$$(200, 36) \implies t = 200\text{ ms}$$

State the maximum qualifying time:
$$\text{Qualifying threshold} = 200\text{ ms}$$

teacher_walkthrough.text:
Remember that faster means smaller time:
$$\text{Target count} = 0.15 \times 240 = 36$$

ai_rubric.observable: Identify that fastest 15% corresponds to the lower 15% tail: 0.15 * 240 = 36.
Identify that CF = 36 corresponds exactly to t = 200 ms.
State maximum qualifying reaction time as 200 ms.

parts.label: a
hints: Median is at $CF = 0.50 \times 300 = 150$, which falls between $(140, 120)$ and $(180, 225)$.
Interpolate median: $140 + \frac{150 - 120}{225 - 120} \times 40 = 140 + \frac{30}{105} \times 40 = 151.43\text{ dollars}$.
The 90th percentile is at $CF = 0.90 \times 300 = 270$, between $(180, 225)$ and $(220, 276)$.

walkthrough.text:
Interpolate median at $CF = 0.50 \times 300 = 150$:
$$\text{Median} = 140 + \frac{150 - 120}{225 - 120} \times (180 - 140) = 140 + \frac{30}{105} \times 40 = 140 + \frac{80}{7} \approx 151.43\text{ dollars}$$

Interpolate 90th percentile at $CF = 0.90 \times 300 = 270$:
$$P_{90} = 180 + \frac{270 - 225}{276 - 225} \times (220 - 180) = 180 + \frac{45}{51} \times 40 = 180 + \frac{600}{17} \approx 215.29\text{ dollars}$$

teacher_walkthrough.text:
Interpolate median at cumulative count 150:
$$\text{Median} = 140 + \frac{30}{105} \times 40 \approx 151.43\text{ dollars}$$

Interpolate 90th percentile at cumulative count 270:
$$P_{90} = 180 + \frac{45}{51} \times 40 \approx 215.29\text{ dollars}$$

ai_rubric.observable: Interpolate median at CF = 150: 140 + (30 / 105) * 40.
Obtain median expenditure = 151.43 dollars (accept 151.40 to 151.50, or 1060/7).
Interpolate 90th percentile at CF = 270: 180 + (45 / 51) * 40 = 215.29 dollars (accept 215.25 to 215.35, or 3660/17).

parts.label: b
hints: Lower quartile is at $CF = 0.25 \times 300 = 75$, between $(100, 45)$ and $(140, 120)$.
Interpolate $Q_1$: $100 + \frac{75 - 45}{120 - 45} \times 40 = 100 + \frac{30}{75} \times 40 = 116\text{ dollars}$.
Upper quartile is at $CF = 0.75 \times 300 = 225$, which is an exact plotted point: $(180, 225)$, so $Q_3 = 180\text{ dollars}$.
Calculate $\text{IQR} = Q_3 - Q_1 = 180 - 116 = 64\text{ dollars}$.

walkthrough.text:
Interpolate lower quartile $Q_1$ at $CF = 0.25 \times 300 = 75$:
$$Q_1 = 100 + \frac{75 - 45}{120 - 45} \times (140 - 100) = 100 + \frac{30}{75} \times 40 = 100 + 16 = 116\text{ dollars}$$

Identify upper quartile $Q_3$ at $CF = 0.75 \times 300 = 225$ directly from the given point $(180, 225)$:
$$Q_3 = 180\text{ dollars}$$

Compute the interquartile range:
$$\text{IQR} = Q_3 - Q_1 = 180 - 116 = 64\text{ dollars}$$

teacher_walkthrough.text:
Interpolate Q1 at cumulative count 75:
$$Q_1 = 100 + 16 = 116\text{ dollars}$$

Read Q3 at cumulative count 225:
$$Q_3 = 180\text{ dollars}$$

Subtract to obtain the IQR:
$$\text{IQR} = 180 - 116 = 64\text{ dollars}$$

ai_rubric.observable: Interpolate Q1 at CF = 75: 100 + (30 / 75) * 40 = 116 dollars.
Identify Q3 directly at CF = 225 as 180 dollars.
Calculate IQR = Q3 - Q1 = 180 - 116 = 64 dollars.

parts.label: c
hints: Interpolate cumulative frequency at $E = 200$: $225 + \frac{200 - 180}{220 - 180} \times 51 = 225 + 25.5 = 250.5$.
Families spending $> 200\text{ dollars}$: $300 - 250.5 = 49.5$.
Interpolate cumulative frequency at $E = 120$ between $(100, 45)$ and $(140, 120)$: $45 + \frac{20}{40} \times 75 = 82.5$.
Find the number of families between $120$ and $200\text{ dollars}$: $250.5 - 82.5 = 168$.
Calculate the probability: $168 / 300 = 0.56$.

walkthrough.text:
Interpolate cumulative frequency at $E = 200$ and find the upper tail count:
$$CF(200) = 225 + \frac{200 - 180}{220 - 180} \times (276 - 225) = 225 + 0.5 \times 51 = 250.5$$
$$\text{Eligible families} = 300 - 250.5 = 49.5\text{ families}$$

Interpolate cumulative frequency at $E = 120$ between $(100, 45)$ and $(140, 120)$:
$$CF(120) = 45 + \frac{120 - 100}{140 - 100} \times (120 - 45) = 45 + 0.5 \times 75 = 82.5$$

Calculate the count and probability for spending between 120 and 200 dollars:
$$\text{Count}(120 \le E \le 200) = 250.5 - 82.5 = 168$$
$$P(120 \le E \le 200) = \frac{168}{300} = \frac{14}{25} = 0.56$$

teacher_walkthrough.text:
Interpolate at 200 dollars and subtract from 300:
$$CF(200) = 250.5 \implies \text{Eligible} = 49.5$$

ai_rubric.observable: Interpolate CF at E = 200 to obtain 250.5, giving eligible families = 300 - 250.5 = 49.5 (accept 49 or 50).
Interpolate CF at E = 120 to obtain 82.5, giving count between 120 and 200 dollars as 250.5 - 82.5 = 168.
Calculate probability = 168 / 300 = 14 / 25 = 0.56.
